title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI gates and quality metric integrations
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: add a lightweight prompt-set regression gate to the eval-harness CI so that PRs touching prompts, generation code paths, or model invocation plumbing surface quality regressions early. This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow and small runner that executes curated prompt sets against a pinned set of model variants and computes quality metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU, BERTScore, and a semantic similarity score). The CI exposes configurable thresholds per-prompt-set and per-metric; if the change causes metric regressions beyond the configured tolerances the check fails and posts a summarized artifact to the PR. Changes: - New workflow: .github/workflows/prompt-regression.yml that runs on PRs touching eval-harness, redwood model-onboarding, and prompt directories. - CI runner: eval-harness/ci/runner.py implements orchestration, cached model outputs, and threshold comparison. - Config: eval-harness/configs/prompt-gates.yaml contains prompt sets, baseline hashes, and per-metric thresholds. - Reporter: eval-harness/ci/reporter.py produces a compact HTML/JSON artifact and posts a check run summary with links to artifacts. - Docs: redwood-docs/docs/evals/prompt-gating.md with how it works and how to opt-in/out for large experiments. - Tests: added unit and integration tests that simulate regressions and flaky model outputs. Deployment notes: the workflow uses a matrix with a single lightweight open model and a small accuracy-focused internal model label to keep runtime < 10m for typical PRs; the runner supports opt-in longer runs for heavyweight regressions. It also supports a local-mode for developers to run the same gating locally. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) - [x] Config format stable and documented - [x] Tests for gating and artifact publishing - [x] Docs updated - [x] CI passes on rerun Known limitations: small prompt sets may not catch all regressions; metric thresholds are conservative by default. Future work (separate PRs): add automated baseline updates, more model variants for broader coverage, and alert integration with Console for post-merge regressions.

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can you clarify how baseline hashes are computed and stored? Also, how do we avoid flakes from nondeterministic decoding?

Ava Martinez (author): Baselines are SHA256 over normalized JSON of the model outputs for each prompt; runner normalizes timestamps and non-deterministic fields. We also have a retry+median strategy and an optional seed override for deterministic decodes.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): The threshold config looks reasonable but we should make it easy to override per-repo to avoid noisy failures for large model experiments.
Ava Martinez (author): Added opt-in per-repo config and documented it. Kept defaults conservative to reduce noise.
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): CI runtime looked high in the first run, can we cache model outputs across runs?
Ava Martinez (author): Implemented a small artifact cache keyed by baseline hash; subsequent runs skip repeated model calls when baseline matches. Reran CI and runtime dropped ~60%.
Liam Chen (reviewer): Approving after tests and flake fixes.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): LGTM — good to land once CI is green.

release_notes: Add prompt-set regression CI gate: runs small curated prompt sets and enforces metric thresholds (ROUGE-L, BLEU, BERTScore, semantic-sim).
Adds config for per-prompt-set thresholds and baseline management.
CI artifacts published to PR for quick triage when a gate fails.
notes: This PR is the first phase of eval-harness CI integration; teams should file follow-ups if their workloads need broader coverage.
